items.title: `.autofocus()` is the ONE spelling: in the browser it REGISTERS the element (no attribute left in the DOM) and the focus scope starts on a registered descendant; on the server it writes the native `autofocus`; a WRITTEN `autofocus` attribute gets a steer to the method, with the reason
items.body:
The owner's design. (1) Browser: `View::autofocus()` records the element in a module-level registry (a `WeakSet<Element>` behind an `external` binding - no expando, nothing held alive) and, outside any scope, keeps today's bounded focus-on-mount (B271). `FocusScope::focus_initial` starts on the FIRST descendant in tree order that is registered; else a hand-written native `[autofocus]` descendant; else the first tabbable; else the panel. No `data-autofocus` marker: A151's marker and `AUTOFOCUS_MARKER` go before they ship.

CHECKED (the owner's question): the scope does NOT have to exist before its content renders. `focus_initial` already walks the root's descendants lazily, at the show, long after the content is built - so a registry it consults per candidate needs no context, no change to `focus_scope`'s API, and no edit to kolt's overlay. (The integrator's first reading - a context the content registers with, which would force scope-before-content - was wrong; the registry also keeps HTML's 'first in tree order' for free, where registration order would not.)

(2) Server: `View::autofocus()` WRITES the native `autofocus` attribute - initial parse is the one place it works and logs nothing. This reverses reactive-46's 'the server drops it'.

(3) A WRITTEN `autofocus` in an element head (`<input autofocus />`, which lowers to `attr("autofocus", ..)`) gets a WARNING: the native attribute only acts at initial parse, and on a later insert Chromium logs 'Autofocus processing was blocked..'; write `.autofocus()`. Quick-fix data to rewrite the attribute to the dotted method in the head. The browser `attr`'s silent rename of `autofocus` goes: an explicit `.attr("autofocus", "")` writes the native attribute, unsteered, for a native `<dialog>`/popover. The server `attr` serves a written `autofocus` as written.

(4) A registered element removed from the document simply is not found by the walk; nothing to unregister.

Pins: both twins; a scope starts on the registered descendant with NO autofocus-ish attribute in the DOM; first-in-tree-order of two; the native fallback; the steer on the element-syntax attribute and not on `.attr(..)`; the server render carries `autofocus`. A kolt patch rewrites its six element-syntax `autofocus` sites to `.autofocus()`.
